I can help with that in a respectful, non-pushy way. Here’s a practical plan to approach him and ask him out without making things awkward.

Steps
- Start with a light, natural conversation next time you see him.
  - Example openers:
    - “Hey, I’m Sana. I’ve been looking for good [genre] book recommendations—do you have any favorites?”
    - “Hi, I’m Sana. I noticed you mentioned [book/author] in the section—what else would you recommend?”
  - Keep it short, friendly, and gauge his interest.

- Build a quick connection.
  - Ask one or two open-ended questions about books, libraries, or study topics.
  - Share a little about your interests to create common ground.

- Read the cues.
  - If he seems engaged, continue talking a bit more.
  - If he keeps the conversation brief or seems distracted, gracefully wrap up and don’t push.

- Ask him out in a low-pressure way.
  - In person: “I’ve enjoyed talking with you. Would you be up for grabbing a coffee after the library closes or sometime this week?”
  - By text (if you have his number): “Hey [Name], it’s Sana from [University]. I really enjoyed our chat about [topic]. Want to grab coffee this weekend?”

- Have a low-pressure backup plan.
  - If he says yes, suggest a simple place and time: “How about Friday after class at [cafe] around [time]?”
  - If he says no or is unsure, respond gracefully: “No worries at all—thanks for the chat today.” Move on politely.

- Safety and boundaries.
  - Meet in a public place.
  - Don’t push for more contact than he’s comfortable with.
  - If you don’t get a positive response, give yourself credit for trying and respect his boundaries.

If you want, tell me more specifics:
- Are you approaching him in person or via message?
- What field are you studying (for context of your conversations)?
- Any topics you know you both enjoy?
